html:
The Kureinji, also called the Keramin, are an Aboriginal people of southwest New South Wales, along the north side of the Murray River between present day Euston and Wentworth.

The Murray and its lakes gave fish, mussels, waterbirds and plant foods, and the river peoples here lived in larger and more settled groups than those of the dry country. Neighbours on the map include the Muthi Muthi to the east, the Paakantyi along the Darling and the Latje Latje across the river.

Overlanders drove stock along the Murray to Adelaide from 1838, and violent clashes followed along the river. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: The Kureinji, also called the Keramin, are an Aboriginal people of southwest New South Wales, along the north side of the Murray River between present day Euston and Wentworth.
